 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The learned High Court Government Pleader accepts notice for the respondent No.1 - State.
2. Sri Madhu R, learned counsel files vakalath on behalf of the respondent No.2.

3. The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
4.

The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband of the respondent No.2, and the accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-laws of the respondent No.2 NC: 2023:KHC:40062 and the accused No.4 is the brother-in-law, and they subjected the respondent No.2 to cruelty both mentally and physically, and a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.

sentences.text:
The parties are present before this Court and have filed an application under Section 320(2) read with Section 482 of Cr.PC, stating that they have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves,
and the respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing the impugned FIR.
The application is placed on record.

6. The petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.2 had filed a petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolving their marriage mutually and the said matter was referred to the Mediation Center.

Before the Mediation Center, the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves and in terms of the settlement, their marriage has been dissolved mutually and a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- was paid towards permanent alimony in favour of the defacto complainant.
The respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing the impugned FIR 7.

Though the offences are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 having agreed to withdraw all the allegations made by her, it would be an futile exercise if the petitioners - accused are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the NC: 2023:KHC:40062 settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.14699/2016 pending on the file of the learned IX Addl. CMM, at Bangalore, is hereby quashed.
